title: Comparison: Supreme Court vs High Court

blocks.content: The writ jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226 is wider than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.

items: Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right, making SC remedy mandatory, whereas Article 226 is a constitutional remedy and discretionary for the High Court.
Supreme Court judges submit resignation to the President; High Court judges also submit resignation to the President, not the State Governor.
A High Court judge can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Supreme Court judge.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Supreme Court operates as the supreme judicial authority under Part V, while High Courts function at the state level under Part VI of the Constitution.
High Courts possess wider writ jurisdiction (Article 226) than the Supreme Court (Article 32) as they can issue writs for both Fundamental Rights and ordinary legal rights.
Judges of the Supreme Court retire at 65 years of age, whereas High Court judges retire at 62 years of age.
The Supreme Court holds exclusive original jurisdiction in federal disputes involving the Centre and states or between states.
Both courts function as Courts of Record with powers to punish for contempt of court.
